scope_assessment: Reviewed the full unified diff against frozen Phase4 base 4485966: new guest avatar metadata/media routes (guest-avatar-http.ts, guest-avatar-runtime.ts, app routes under /api/guest/avatar and /guest-avatar-media), the new guest-avatar contract (guest-avatar.ts), GuestAvatarPreview.tsx and its integration into GuestBooking.tsx step 2 only, AvatarFitPreview.tsx's scoped-src extension, avatar-runtime.ts (dedicated avatar_read pool), staff avatar-media-http.ts's permission tightening, PostgresAvatarVisuals' refactor onto the new avatar_current_visuals view/avatar_visual_derivative function, migration 0032, scripts/avatar-read-role.ts, and all associated unit/PG/browser test files. Confirmed by hash/byte comparison that 0001-0031 are unchanged (migration-hashes.json matches the shown migration files) and that GuestBooking.tsx's only change is the added GuestAvatarPreview call inside the step===2 candidate block; no other business file (guest/service.ts, hold/quote services, payment, staff-auth) is touched except the read-path swap in avatar-media/[visualId]/[hash]/route.ts and preview/avatar/page.tsx from publicRuntime() to avatarRuntime(). Traced control flow by hand through guestAvatarHandler -> loadGuestAvatar -> loadAvatarPreview -> authorizeBookingActor, through avatarDerivative -> PostgresAvatarVisuals.readBytes -> avatar_visual_derivative(), and through the 0032 view definition against the removed inline SQL in avatar-visuals.ts to confirm semantic equivalence plus the clock_timestamp() tightening.

findings.title: Guest avatar metadata/media routes bypass the existing GuestSecurity rate-limiter used by other /api/guest/* endpoints
findings.counterexample: Every other guest surface is composed through guestHandler(), which in production requires a GuestSecurity object and calls security.service.guard(peer) (a real per-peer/global sliding-window limiter) before doing any work. guestAvatarHandler is invoked directly from the route file with no equivalent wrapper, guard call, or window/peer budget of any kind; a caller holding a single valid guest cookie can issue an unbounded number of metadata/media GETs.
findings.impact: Low in this milestone: the routes still fail closed to null/404 in Production (avatarRuntime()/publicRuntime() both return null when NODE_ENV==='production'), so this is only reachable in the local development runtime that this phase explicitly targets, and each request is bounded (single owned draft/preview, small WebP payload). It would become a real availability/DB-load concern the moment a future phase activates this route outside local development without adding an equivalent guard.
findings.test_coverage: No PG or browser check in e2e.log/local-e2e.json exercises a request-volume/rate limit against the avatar metadata or media routes; the existing GuestSecurity rate-limit tests (readiness/guest-security.ts) cover only the guestHandler-composed endpoints.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Either explicitly document that these are unthrottled local-development-only endpoints identical in trust level to other unauthenticated-but-cookie-scoped GETs, or wrap guestAvatarHandler with the same GuestSecurity.guard(peer) call used by guestHandler before any future non-local exposure.
findings.required_proof: A local PG/browser check asserting the actual per-peer/global request budget behavior (or explicit absence of one) for /api/guest/avatar/* and /guest-avatar-media/*, turning this into a tested, explicit decision.

historical_finding_dispositions.reason: 0032's avatar_visual_guard() now raises 23514 on any UPDATE that changes any of id, layer, avatar_type, match_kind, model_id, variant_id, season, ski_length_cm, media_id, derivative_sha256, revision_id, release_id or created_at (full 13-field ROW comparison), leaving only state/sort_order/anchor/position/updated_at mutable. Verified by direct inspection of the trigger body and by the 13 individual 'binding immutable: <field>' PG assertions in phase5-upgrade.ts/upgrade.log, each of which rejects the specific field with code 23514. This closes the original concern (schema permitted binding-field UPDATE with no writer/editor route relying on read-time containment alone); the guard now enforces immutability at the schema layer itself.

mapAvatarVisualization/media.ts/avatar_current_visuals are unchanged in their all-or-nothing zero-artwork behavior: zero/invalid visuals still yield no renderer and no ratio-only fallback (avatar-visualization.test.ts 'zero visuals/all inactive/rights denied leave exact business object unchanged'; avatar-renderer.test.ts 'absent invalid and zero artwork do not invent renderer or images'). This remains the Owner's explicit scoped product choice for this milestone, not an independently closed finding; no new artwork exists to test the alternative path.

A genuinely narrow, purpose-built avatar_read role now exists (scripts/avatar-read-role.ts) granting only SELECT on the security_barrier avatar_current_visuals view and EXECUTE on avatar_visual_derivative(uuid,text) -- verified by direct grant inspection and by ten distinct PG rejection tests (workspace JSON, raw media bytes, immutable revisions, unfiltered visual metadata, guest credentials, saved business preview, visual/business/workspace writes, DDL all rejected with 42501). This is real, tested, and is now the actual role used by both staff (avatar-media-http.ts via avatarRuntime()) and guest (guest-avatar-runtime.ts) code paths, replacing the previous ad-hoc readPool usage. However, the original finding's concern was about production privilege minimization for a hosted/runtime role; no Production Avatar role or Production activation exists in this phase (avatarRuntime()/publicRuntime() both fail closed under NODE_ENV==='production'), so the underlying production-scope question this finding raised remains unresolved by construction, not by proof. Counted as still OPEN pending an actual Production role design in a future phase.

avatar-media-http.ts's allowed() now requires ['BOOKING_VIEW','HOLD_VIEW','QUOTE_VIEW'].every(...), byte-for-byte matching the permission set enforced by /preview/avatar/page.tsx. The exact counterexample from the original finding (a principal holding BOOKING_VIEW only, with HOLD_VIEW and QUOTE_VIEW explicitly denied) is now directly tested in phase5-e2e.ts ('PHASE4-1 exact counterexample: BOOKING_VIEW only denies preview and bytes') and passes, along with the two single-permission-missing variants. The asymmetry the finding identified no longer exists in the reviewed code.

guest_integration_assessment: GuestAvatarPreview is wired into GuestBooking.tsx only inside the step===2 candidate-review block (one instance per member row), never in step 0/1/3; it fetches '/api/guest/avatar/'+path via a plain same-origin credentialed GET on mount/path change, catches failures silently with no retry, and renders null if the payload is absent/empty -- confirmed by direct code reading and by 'optional artwork HTTP failure does not fail candidate step or invent art' and 'ordinary GuestBooking without approved artwork still previews candidates' passing without [data-avatar-stage]. Appearance switching (button click) is local React state only; AvatarFitPreview/GuestAvatarPreview issue no fetch/POST on direction or appearance change, matching visualBusinessPosts:0 in every log and the explicit metadataRequests-count assertion in phase5-e2e.ts. Direction remains driven by the existing candidate radios (directions state), and the existing explicit-selection/acceptedModelPolicy/checkbox flow into /selection is byte-identical to Phase4's guest flow. loadGuestAvatar strictly binds to the caller's own current guest_drafts row (id+revision+preview_id) resolved from the HttpOnly cookie, never from the URL-supplied scope alone, and re-reads after loadAvatarPreview to reject changes that occurred during the load. offeredAvatarVisual further requires the requested visualId+digest to appear in the specific member's currently offered candidates (not merely 'eligible' globally), correctly denying 'eligible garment outside this saved member offer'.
media_security_assessment: guestAvatarHandler enforces GET-only, empty query string, prefix-exact path, sec-fetch-site!=='cross-site', exact segment count, and strict UUID/digest regexes before any auth/DB work (confirmed by 5 'invalid guest image shape denies before auth/DB' unit tests asserting zero loads/reads). avatarDerivative performs its own before/after eligibility check around the actual SHA-256 recomputation and validAvatarRaster (unchanged bounded WebP/alpha/physical-crop validator from Phase4), and the outer handler performs a further independent before/after full reload+offeredAvatarVisual canonical-equality check, giving three layered reauthorization points around one byte read -- verified against the three 'race after bytes: revoked context/replaced preview/replaced grant' unit tests and the eleven PG 'denies old guest image URL' scenarios (rights revoked/expired/internal-only/unprocessed/release changed/purpose removed/immutable revision mismatch/digest retarget/release entry removed/duplicate metadata/inactive visual). Bytes are additionally gated inside the SECURITY DEFINER avatar_visual_derivative SQL function itself (re-checks avatar_current_visuals membership and a 4MiB cap at the database layer), independent of the application-layer checks. All responses are private,no-store, Vary: Cookie, CSP sandbox, nosniff, noindex; every denial path returns an indistinguishable empty 404 regardless of failure cause. next/image is used with unoptimized (confirmed by both unit test and absence of _next/image in captured requests), so the public image optimizer is never invoked for rights-sensitive bytes. Guest routes cannot reach the staff-only /avatar-media/ URL or broaden the existing public /media/ route (explicitly tested).
migration_role_assessment: 0032 is strictly additive; 0001-0031 file hashes are unchanged per migration-hashes.json against the shown migration sources. The rewritten avatar_visual_guard() enforces full 13-field binding immutability (superset of 0031's id/created_at-only check), tested field-by-field. avatar_current_visuals is a security_barrier view fully qualifying all underlying tables (public.*), confirmed resistant to temp-table shadowing by direct test, and moves the rights_until comparison from a caller-supplied timestamp to clock_timestamp() -- a genuine tightening, confirmed by 'current-rights check cannot be bypassed using an old caller timestamp'. avatar_visual_derivative is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned, fully-qualified search_path, PUBLIC execute revoked, and independently re-verifies current eligibility and a 4MiB size cap inside the function body. scripts/avatar-read-role.ts grants only SELECT on the view and EXECUTE on the function to a NOLOGIN-safe, NOSUPERUSER/NOCREATEDB/NOCREATEROLE/NOINHERIT/NOBYPASSRLS role, verified by ten explicit rejection tests plus role-flag/pg_auth_members inspection. The narrow view preserves exact PREMIUM model/variant/season/length semantics (re-verified live against ledger_variants/ledger_models rather than cached), confirmed via the dedicated PG test that inserts a real exact-match variant and checks both correct resolution and rejection of mismatched season/length/model/variant.
authorization_business_assessment: loadAvatarPreview is unchanged in its authorize-then-owner-scoped-select-then-reauthorize-with-stores pattern, now generalized to BookingActor (staff or guest) via authorizeBookingActor, which for guests requires the caller's contextId/subject/tokenHash to match a live, non-revoked, non-expired guest_contexts row joined to booking_actors -- a distinct capability path from staff sessions, never staff impersonation. No route in this diff calls RecommendationService.preview/select/resume from the avatar path; GuestBooking's existing explicit-selection flow into /selection, /accept-price and /checkout is untouched. avatar-media-http.ts's permission check is now aligned exactly with the preview page's three-permission requirement, closing PHASE4-1. The only new DB write surface possibility (avatar_visuals) still has no writer/editor route in this diff; the sole application-level change to avatar-visuals.ts is the read-only eligible()/readBytes() refactor onto the new view/function.
validation_assessment: Self-reported counts (253 unit / 97 real local PostgreSQL / 26 browser, all PASS) are Codex self-validation, not independently re-executed (tools disabled per this review's scope). I read tests/avatar/phase5-e2e.ts, phase5-upgrade.ts, and tests/unit/guest-avatar.test.ts in full and confirmed each named assertion actually exercises the claimed condition rather than merely logging PASS -- e.g. the 11 'denies old guest image URL' PG cases genuinely mutate a structuredClone of the base ContentWorkflowState and restore it after each assertion, and the three 'race after bytes' unit tests genuinely swap the boundary's load() implementation mid-flight to simulate a real TOCTOU window. The retained preparation/ logs (initial TEST_APP_START_FAILED, second ERR_ASSERTION on RSC Vary header, third TimeoutError, fourth missing the PHASE4-1 exact counterexample, and the upgrade-phase view-not-updatable ERR_ASSERTION) are consistent with, and corroborate, the corrections listed in validation.json's preparationCorrections array; nothing in the final logs appears retrofitted to hide an unresolved failure. Migration hash equality was independently verified against the migration-hashes.json entries shown in this snapshot. As with all static review, I cannot verify that the actual CI run produced exactly these log files unmodified; this is the accepted residual risk under tests_executed:false and is not treated as missing evidence given the source code fully explains and reproduces the reported behavior.
